#5219. After dodging death, battery startup Our Next Energy is now going public

It’s never been easy to run a battery startup in the U.S. There have been more failures than successes over the last 20 years, and whipsawing federal policy has caused more than a few battery companies to shut shop.

Not all of them die, though. Our Next Energy (ONE) had some close calls, but soon it will go public via SPAC, the company exclusively told TechCrunch.

ONE says it is valued at $600 million pre-money, and it expects the merger with Wen Acquisition Corp. will bring $400 million in gross proceeds assuming no redemptions. The combined company will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker “ONEE,” and the pro forma implied equity value is $1 billion.

Over the years, ONE has raised $483 million, according to PitchBook, and at one point was valued at $1.3 billion. It has also received tens of millions of dollars in incentives tied to investments and job creation in Michigan.

ONE is the brainchild of former Ford and Apple engineer Mujeeb Ijaz, who designed a way for electric vehicles to draw power from two batteries of different chemistries. In ONE’s first setup, it paired lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) and with a manganese-rich chemistry, which would let each chemistry play to its strengths: LFP could be used day in, day out, while the more fragile but energy-dense, manganese-rich one would work for long, infrequent road trips. An initial prototype traveled over 600 miles on a single charge.

But the EV market didn’t take off as quickly as anticipated, and automakers wanted to buy at lower prices (usually from China). Both of those reasons helped sink ONE’s first attempt at a Series C in late 2023. The startup had to lay off a chunk of its staff, and eventually vacated its lease for a planned $1.6 billion factory in Michigan.

The rough patch led to Ijaz’s ouster as CEO in December 2023, only to have him return to the position in March 2025 after a new round of funding closed. (His brother’s investment firm co-led the round.)

Part of the critique aimed at ONE during Ijaz’s first tenure as CEO was that the company spent too much time developing new products instead of focusing on one or two, as most startups tend to do. When Ijaz came back to the helm last year, he said that ONE would leave the automotive market and focus on grid-scale batteries.

ONE isn’t alone in pivoting away from vehicle batteries. American automakers, which had similarly rosy views of EV adoption, also bet big on battery factories and supply chains. When sales didn’t pop in the U.S. like they have in China or Europe, they had to find an outlet for that capacity, and the grid started looking like the obvious target once it started groaning under the weight of AI data centers. Both Ford and GM have announced their own energy storage products.

Many new grid-scale batteries use LFP, which is safer and cheaper than those used in most EVs in the U.S., and Ijaz saw an opportunity for ONE there as well. “We go back to the origins of LFP in this country and even to some of the factories that are in China,” he said. Indeed, just over a decade ago Ijaz led the automotive division at A123 Systems, the company that first commercialized the chemistry.

Soon, Ijaz saw other opportunities for ONE’s batteries, including defense and locomotives.

The defense play isn’t surprising. Nearly every battery company I talk with these days mentions defense, in part because it’s a market that Chinese companies can’t play in. Building an American supply chain means that a company can sell batteries at a premium, shielded as they are from Chinese competition. It’s a higher-margin market, though much smaller than EVs.

My recent conversation with Ijaz last week was the first time I’d heard a company pitch rail companies as potential customers, though. Ijaz said ONE is “finding a lot of traction in” that market. The company has built a hybrid locomotive that uses a 2.8 megawatt-hour battery, and another he calls a micro-hybrid, which uses a smaller battery to start the diesel engine faster, similar to a stop-start system on a fossil fuel car or truck.

“Our customers are seeing a 50% improvement in diesel fuel consumption, which is a big deal,” Ijaz said.

Currently, ONE has three business lines, which could be a sign of its old culture creeping back into the picture. But Ijaz said the addition of defense and rail were driven by the bottom line: Grid-scale battery customers are also “very much like automotive customers, where they were willing to buy from China as long as the price was low enough,” he said.

“Believe me, I would have loved to have made that grid business into the single business of the company. But the customers would look and then be taken away to a Chinese option because of the pricing, and the tariffs also leading them to that conclusion,” Ijaz said. “And so we decided that we needed a more durable market, and we looked for who in the customer base valued an American battery company.”

Today, ONE operates a pack assembly plant in Novi, Michigan, which can put together packs from cells at a rate of 3 gigawatt-hours per year. The plant uses cells from China-based and non-China-based suppliers, as well as ONE’s own cells from a smaller factory nearby, which is currently being upgraded to make 50 megawatt-hours of batteries per year.

In its investor pitch, which TechCrunch has reviewed, ONE distills its business lines into defense and rail. Drones and submarines make up the majority of what ONE sees as a $16.2 billion market. Defense-focused data centers get lumped in there, too, contributing $4.1 billion to the defense business. (That appears to be the main outlet for grid-scale batteries.) The other line, which serves the rail industry, is expected to be worth $28.2 billion.

Both markets are sizable, but they pale in comparison to the EV sector, which is worth about $73 billion today, and could grow to $200 billion by the end of the decade, according to Grand View Research. This year, ONE expects to bring in $30 million in revenue, and hopes to make double that next year. The company said it has $200 million in binding, multi-year contracts with railroads and defense contractors.

ONE hasn’t closed the door on the automotive industry, Ijaz said. “Automotive still is a race to the bottom on margins,” he said. “As time goes on, if we win an automotive contract for any purpose, we’ll take a look at it, but not at any cost.”

ONE’s pitch centers on the so-called foreign entity of concern (FEOC) restrictions: The U.S. government can’t buy batteries made in China or those made using minerals from China-controlled supply chains, so ONE will target them first.

But it’s a pitch that many battery companies are making today. Whether investors buy into ONE’s vision will depend on if they think the company has parted with its tumultuous past and found a focus. It will need both to succeed in the increasingly cutthroat battery industry.

Despite the market downturn, XRP Ledger is showing a somewhat reassuring trend: the price has bounced toward the $1 mark and, thankfully, the move is followed by a volume uptick, which could start a proper recovery rally.

XRP is trading at $0.96 after dipping to $0.89. The $1 threshold, which essentially enables a rapid decrease if broken, gave in on November 14. It's the first time XRP traded below $1 since mid-August.

The market is bearish, and the RSI dropped into the 20-ish zone, which is considered "extremely oversold". Moving averages are still rapidly diverging, which might further reinforce the bearish dynamic.

Even if XRP reclaims the round number, bulls might still stay sidelined. If bulls somehow wake up, a recovery toward $1.2 is the main priority, as it's the level where a lot of investors accumulated XRP in the past.

On the other hand, the Ledger shows elevated activity, with the potential to go further and reclaim levels we haven't seen in the bear market. Still, elevated activity during a prolonged market descent is not something we should just shake off.

According to on-chain data, payment volume on the XRP Ledger reached around 1.1 billion XRP, up 139.9%. Active accounts went up by 154.5%, reaching 42,300. Payments volume growth is substantial, but not record-breaking by any means.

The XRP Ledger has seen substantial growth in various on-chain metrics, which, unfortunately, does not give the price enough support. A lot of the Ledger activity might be automated, driven by either trading bots or sophisticated LLM models. The market is mostly driven by speculative interest rather than fundamental network usage.

The activity of investors who are trying to cash out or pull their holdings away from exchanges could be the key here. Growing payments volume most likely reflects growing fear among investors, as some of them move funds to exchanges in order to liquidate their coins.

Payments volume rises, but so does the bear market pressure, with a possibility of a further downturn that could make things worse than they already are.

The price of Bitcoin has dropped by around 19% over the 50 days before the Nasdaq debut of Anthropic, and the decline is similar to the one that Bitcoin had ahead of the SpaceX listing in June. At press time, Bitcoin is trading at $65,450, according to TradingView. Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on Nov. 13, and it dropped below $67,000 over the weekend.

Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, is set to start trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Nov. 19. The AI company is offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each and aims to raise up to $64.4 billion in the IPO. At the top of the range, Anthropic would be valued at around $1.4 trillion, and the company has also arranged a $26 billion private placement.

SpaceX raised a record $75 billion in its IPO this summer, so the Anthropic listing is close to it in size. Before the SpaceX IPO, the price of Bitcoin also went down by around 19%.

Fundstrat managing partner Tom Lee called the current drawdown a temporary rotation of money into mega-IPOs, as investors sell liquid assets to buy shares in the largest offerings of the year.

After SpaceX started trading on Nasdaq, the price of Bitcoin kept falling for another 18 days. After that, Bitcoin went up, and 100 days after the IPO, it was 28% above its close on the day of the listing.

If Bitcoin repeats this pattern after the Anthropic IPO, it could reach $90,000 by the end of February 2027, according to Strive CEO Matt Cole.

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao shared the comparison of the two charts on X and called Cole's numbers "an interesting analysis." Still, some users in the replies under the post blamed the drop of Bitcoin on selling by Binance, not on the IPO calendar.

The Deutsche Bank leak of over 15 million files sent the German lender's stock dropping roughly 5% to 6% in European trading.

Bank executives hid a 2017 tax data breach involving 1,586 accounts, including Donald Trump's, by internally relabeling it a "digital unit release."

Internal reports flagged $582 million across 3,200 Jeffrey Epstein transactions, more than double the $250 million found by Senate investigators.

Traditional banks love lecturing crypto about compliance, yet the massive Deutsche Bank whistleblower leak tells a very different story.

Over 15 million confidential files just hit the spotlight, sending shares in Germany’s largest lender tumbling roughly 5% to 6%. While headlines mash Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein together, the files don’t link their money. Instead, they expose two separate compliance trainwrecks at one institution.

Back in March 2017, a relationship manager accidentally emailed year-end tax statements for 1,586 private accounts, including Trump’s, to a single client’s accountant. Thankfully, that accountant deleted the massive file without opening it.

Rather than coming clean, executives buried the blunder by calling it a “digital unit release” internally. Worse yet, the bank placed Trump’s accounts under an encrypted, restricted protocol codenamed “Novus Ordo” after his 2016 win.

Inside Deutsche Bank: Leak Reveals Flagged Transfers Linked to Trump’s Baku EntitiesA massive cross-border journalism investigation published today, dubbed "Inside Deutsche Bank," has exposed internal records detailing how #Germany’s largest lender handled suspicious financial… pic.twitter.com/PZJvn8SXWH

They also told Congress they found no Russia ties for Trump, despite previously flagging a suspicious 2014 transaction tied to DT Marks Baku LLC in Azerbaijan.

Meanwhile, the bank’s handling of convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein looks even uglier. Deutsche Bank onboarded him in 2013 despite his 2008 conviction. Only after his 2019 arrest did the lender file 21 Suspicious Activity Reports flagging roughly $582 million across 3,200 transactions.

That’s more than double the $250 million Senate investigators previously uncovered. Those transfers included payments to women, suspected charity misuse, and large sums involving associates like Leon Black.

🚨The Financial Times’ reports that Deutsche Bank filed 21 suspicious activity reports in the U.S. back in 2019 covering about 3,200 Epstein linked payments valued at $582 million, including payments to women and transfers from Leon Black and Glenn Dubin. The report cites a… https://t.co/THJmovv8lS

Beyond high-profile names, two whistleblowers leaked 15.6 million records to expose systemic anti-money laundering rot. Management even voted in 2021 to expand Russian business despite compliance warnings, alongside details of an alleged €1.7 billion laundering network.

At the same time, the bank failed to drop 28,000 high-risk clients flagged by early 2018 because executives complained strict rules were “breaking our revenue neck.”

Unsurprisingly, management isn’t disputing the Deutsche Bank documents, claiming these incidents are historical and pointing to €7 billion spent on risk controls between 2019 and 2025.

Yet for anyone watching crypto get regulated to death, this legacy mess proves big banks simply treat fines as the cost of doing business.

#5215. Why Is XRP Bleeding More Than Bitcoin, Ether, and Solana in November Sell-Off? Analyst Cites 3 Brutal Reasons

While Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana have also come under bearish pressure during November’s broader crypto market sell-off, XRP is taking a particularly brutal beating, leaving investors wondering why the token is underperforming its biggest rivals. According to prominent analyst EGRAG Crypto, the weakness is no coincidence, pointing to three key factors that could explain XRP’s sharper decline and signal why the token may continue struggling as bearish sentiment grips the market.

Crypto analyst EGRAG Crypto has highlighted XRP’s worsening performance against Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL) amid November’s broader cryptocurrency market drawdown. In a Nov. 10 post on X, the pundit noted the striking difference in losses since November 4, showing that Ripple’s XRP has suffered the steepest decline among the four major cryptocurrencies.

According to EGRAG Crypto’s figures, XRP has plunged 23.4% since November 4, significantly more than ETH’s 18.2% decline and SOL’s 17% drop. BTC has demonstrated greater resilience, losing just 10.4% over the same period.

The figures raise an important question: Why is XRP bleeding considerably more than its major competitors? EGRAG Crypto has pointed to three possible factors behind the token’s disproportionate weakness, offering a closer look at the selling pressure weighing on the Ripple-linked token.

The first factor is leveraged long liquidations, which EGRAG assigns a 30% probability. According to the analyst, forced liquidations of bullish positions, combined with weak buying demand, could be accelerating XRP’s fall. When leveraged traders are forced to close their positions during a downturn, the resulting selling pressure can trigger further losses and deepen an existing market correction.

The second possibility, which carries a 20% probability, is selling by early XRP holders. EGRAG suggests that longtime investors, often referred to as OGs, could be taking profits and rotating their capital into other cryptocurrencies. Such activity could increase selling pressure on XRP, particularly if large holders decide to reduce their exposure amid uncertain market conditions.

Finally, EGRAG assigns the highest probability, 50%, to what the expert describes as market manipulation or a deliberate liquidity hunt. Under this scenario, sharp price movements could be designed to trigger stop-loss orders and force weaker traders out of their positions before a potential recovery. The analyst believes this could explain why XRP is experiencing disproportionately heavy selling compared with other major cryptocurrencies.

Notably, these percentages represent EGRAG Crypto’s personal probability-based assessment rather than independently verified evidence of the causes behind XRP’s decline.

Beyond identifying the possible reasons behind XRP’s sharper decline, EGRAG Crypto has also highlighted several important price levels that could determine the token’s next move. The analyst identified the $1.00-$1.04 range as a critical stabilization zone, suggesting that holding this area could help XRP establish a floor amid the ongoing selling pressure.

On the upside, EGRAG believes bulls must first reclaim the $1.15 level before targeting $1.25. A recovery above these thresholds could signal improving buying momentum and offer some relief to investors after the recent losses.

Sharing a personal assessment, EGRAG Crypto said the ongoing price action appears more consistent with market manipulation designed to frighten newer investors into selling. However, the analyst raised a bigger question about whale activity, questioning whether deep-pocketed XRP holders are using the downturn to accumulate more tokens or adding to the selling pressure by offloading their holdings.

Ultimately, how whales respond to the current market weakness could offer important clues about XRP’s next direction. If large holders are absorbing the available supply, the sell-off could eventually lose momentum. Conversely, continued whale selling could make an already difficult recovery even harder for the sixth-largest cryptocurrency.

#5214. Crypto Traders Blame Binance for Bitcoin Drop, But Data Points to Coinbase

According to CoinGlass, the cumulative volume delta (CVD) on the Coinbase spot market reached -$1.08 billion between Oct. 31 and Nov. 15. CVD shows the difference between the volume of market buy orders and market sell orders, and a negative CVD means that sellers were more active on the exchange.

Over the same period, the CVD on the spot markets of OKX, Bybit and Binance stood at $240.3 million, $65.17 million and $51.88 million, respectively, so buyers were more active on these three exchanges.

The price of Bitcoin went down from $81,188 on Nov. 4 to $61,956 on Nov. 14, according to CoinGlass data, and the decline amounted to around 24%. On Sunday, Bitcoin recovered to around $65,400.

The data comes amid claims that Binance has been pushing the price of Bitcoin down. The exchange lost $6.4 billion in a hack on Oct. 29, and some users on X then claimed that Binance was selling crypto to cover its losses. Two weeks after the attack, Binance published a Proof of Reserves report that showed client balances on the exchange were fully backed.

This week, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao shared a comparison of Bitcoin charts ahead of the SpaceX and Anthropic IPOs and called it "an interesting analysis." Several users in the replies to his post blamed the drop in Bitcoin on selling by Binance.

Binance is the largest crypto exchange by trading volume, and a large share of futures liquidations takes place on the platform. On Nov. 13, crypto exchanges liquidated 187,389 traders for a total of $1.65 billion in 24 hours, and 88% of that amount came from long positions, according to CoinGlass. Still, the CVD on the Binance spot market has stayed positive since Oct. 31.

Coinbase is the custodian for most U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, including BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, and many U.S. institutional investors trade on the platform through Coinbase Prime.

Anthropic is set to start trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19, and the selling on Coinbase comes ahead of the listing. Fundstrat managing partner Tom Lee has called the recent drawdown in Bitcoin a temporary rotation of money into mega-IPOs, and in the 50 days before the Anthropic IPO, Bitcoin has lost around 18%.

The CVD on Coinbase fell most sharply between Nov. 10 and Nov. 14, and Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 during this period, according to CoinGlass data.

She holds a bachelor’s degree in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University. During her tenure as CFO, Nvidia’s revenue grew dramatically from roughly $4Bn to over $200Bn as the company became the dominant force in AI accelerators.

The mark price has dropped from near or above $170–$175 to the mid-$150s, settling around $158–$160 by November 12, representing roughly a 9–11% decline in the most recent sessions alone and larger cumulative losses from pre-scandal highs.

XRP price saw a sell-off over the weekend, with liquidations accelerating in the last 24 hours. At the time of writing, XRP was down 3.43% in the last 24 hours to $0.969 and down 17% weekly.

Onchain data platform CoinGlass seeks to answer why XRP's price is down. Its analysis, generated from the past 24 hours of futures, spot and ETF data, points to three indicators that help explain the pressure on XRP.

First is a 'long squeeze,' which increased selling pressure on the price. Long traders have taken the biggest hit during the latest decline. CoinGlass data shows that XRP long liquidations reached $43.17 million over the past 24 hours, accounting for about 91% of total liquidations.

Second, open interest has fallen as traders, largely longs, close positions. XRP open interest has fallen 5.53% in the past 24 hours to $2.03 billion.

Thirdly, XRP is currently in negative funding at -0.0082%. Negative funding in perpetual futures markets means that short sellers are paying long sellers to keep positions open, a sign traders are bearish on the market.

XRP fell for 10 straight days from November 5 to November 14, 2026. Price lost momentum after losing the daily MA 200 at the close of October. The cryptocurrency lost another crucial support in early October, the daily MA 50, weakening bulls.

Stablecoin supply is shrinking fast, dropping $17 billion over the last month, the steepest drop since 2022. As holders swap stablecoins to fiat, they drain buying power from BTC and crypto, analysts at Glassnode said.

It will be watched if buying power returns to the market; according to Bitwise CEO Matt Hougan, "There will be a big buying opportunity at some point, but it's hard to say when."

The daily RSI has entered oversold levels, with the possibility of a relief rally in the coming session. Such a recovery, if sustained, will target the daily MA 50 and 200 at $1.25 and $1.30. Further downside is expected to find support at $0.77.

#5211. U.S. Department of Energy Bets on XRP Ledger for Blockchain-Based Energy Market Settlements

The DOE is exploring Ripple’s ledger for energy-market trade settlements, a development showing the protocol is becoming a serious contender in the RWA space.

The global financial world continues to move towards one of its biggest transformations – tokenization of RWAs. This has been further revealed by the U.S. Department of Energy’s decision to utilize the XRP protocol to build digital settlements for energy trades.

In a statement on its platform, the agency said it is building an energy settlement infrastructure on the XRPL.

The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) is a government agency responsible for advancing America’s energy security through reliable, clean, and cost-effective energy. In an official communication, the federal department disclosed that it is using the XRP protocol to develop blockchain applications tailored to energy market needs.

As stated in the report, the entity is developing infrastructure to enable digital trade and settlement of electricity and energy transactions based on the XRPL. By using the protocol, the agency wants to improve the efficiency of energy transactions and charge settlements. It is utilizing the ledger to build on-chain utility for energy assets, linking electricity usage to RWA trades.

The development shows that XRPL is rapidly becoming the top blockchain choice for powering RWAs. This shows that rising interest in tokenization is no longer a fad. Big corporations are already developing systems that bridge TradFi with the on-chain world.

The DOE has joined several prominent corporations, believing in the capability of on-chain-based offerings. This demonstrates how TradFi offerings are being innovatively operated, traded, and managed on on-chain networks.

It’s clear evidence that Ripple’s ledger is becoming a vital settlement architecture for RWAs due to its seamless payment network, swift settlement, and affordable fees.

RWAs require strong ecosystems for swift, affordable transfers of utilities. Ripple’s architecture makes it convenient for such digital utilities and institutional capital transfers. Its robust liquidity bridge also makes it a top candidate, allowing utilities to transit effortlessly across various markets.

Validators have also been told to shut down their nodes from September 10, while the project plans to redirect future token emissions toward its new AI-focused venture, “The Remix Economy.”

In Bitcoin news this week, the question is no longer whether the market is scared. It is whether Extreme Fear means the bottom is close, and what the daily and weekly charts say.

The slide started on Thursday afternoon, when Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. It picked up speed after midnight UTC, when Bitcoin broke below the $72,727 low from Tuesday and kept falling.

Extreme Fear sounds like a buy signal. History says it usually comes early. We found every time since 2018 that the index first dropped to 20 or lower after at least a month without such a reading. There were 16, and we followed Bitcoin for 90 days after each.

The most recent case fits the pattern. Extreme Fear first appeared on June 3 at $64,014, and Bitcoin still fell another 8.5% before it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1. Then it rallied to $87,396 in September.

For anyone reading this Bitcoin news as a buy signal, Extreme Fear says the bottom is getting closer. It has rarely said the bottom is here. A move to the 2026 lows would match the median path.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, Bitcoin sits far below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA is at $78,226 and the 200-day EMA at $76,325.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, the key level is the 200-week EMA at $69,555. Bitcoin trades just below it, and the week closes on Sunday.

That line matters. Bitcoin closed below the 200-week EMA for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of 2026’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

The overnight flush did part of the work a bottom needs: leverage came out and funding turned negative.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Chandler Fang, founder of AI payments startup t54.ai, has said that the company's x402 Facilitator on the XRP Ledger (XRPL) has processed more than 10 million AI agent transactions. Fang made the comments in an interview that the XRPL Foundation published on X on November 15, and the interviewer put the number of these payments at 11.7 million.

According to Fang, XRPL had almost no transactions made by AI agents three or four months before the interview, which was recorded at XRP Seoul 2026. "The entire volume got ramped up very quickly in the three months," he said.

The x402 Facilitator works as a bridge between AI agents and payments, and agents can use XRP or the RLUSD stablecoin to move money without a separate wallet setup for every agent. Fang said that more than 200 merchants are already on the network.

According to Fang, the most common use case is paying for AI compute. Instead of paying $20 to $200 a month for an AI subscription, an agent can pay around $1 or 50 cents for a single task. "Instead, they can purchase this single compute for about $1, or 50 cents, and it can be settled on the XRPL," Fang said.

Fang said that such payments have low value and high frequency, so the high throughput and low fees of XRPL give the network an advantage. He also expects agent payments to move into real-life purchases over the next few quarters. "We have the coffee shop right outside our booth, right? And we are trying to empower users to use XRP and agent payments to finish a real-life transaction," Fang said.

According to Fang, trust is the main issue for agent payments, and t54.ai's Trustline product focuses on risk management for the financial activity of AI agents. He compared the service with the chargeback feature of credit cards. "So there is no lawsuit. It is a similar experience for agents," Fang said.

t54.ai is also part of Mastercard's agentic payment program, where the startup is responsible for risk management. The x402 Facilitator processes transactions based on Mastercard Verifiable Intent, a protocol that verifies the behavior of AI agents.

Fang said that t54.ai, Ripple and Mastercard are in talks about a three-way collaboration, and the first results will be shown at an upcoming hackathon.

"The ten million transactions are just a starting point. I think next year you should expect a lot more transactions. Maybe even more transactions settled on XRPL will be done by AI agents than by humans," Fang said.

#5203. XRP, Dogecoin, and Solana Doomed? Billionaire Tim Draper Predicts Altcoins Will Be Absorbed By Bitcoin — Here’s Why

Could Ripple’s XRP, Dogecoin, and Solana eventually lose their place in the crypto market as Bitcoin strengthens its dominance? Billionaire investor Tim Draper believes the future of cryptocurrencies could look very different, predicting that altcoins will eventually be absorbed by Bitcoin.

Draper’s bold forecast raises fresh questions about the long-term survival of major digital assets and whether BTC’s growing influence could ultimately leave even established altcoins struggling to remain relevant.

Tim Draper has drawn a striking comparison between Bitcoin’s potential dominance and Microsoft’s rise to power in the software industry, arguing that the OG crypto could eventually absorb innovations pioneered by competing digital assets.

In a recent post on X, Draper suggested that Bitcoin could follow a similar path to Microsoft, which built its dominance not necessarily by inventing popular software applications but by incorporating successful innovations into its broader ecosystem.

To illustrate his argument, Draper pointed to Microsoft’s handling of early software pioneers such as Lotus 1-2-3 and WordPerfect. Although these companies helped establish demand for spreadsheet and word-processing applications, Microsoft eventually introduced Excel and Word and integrated both into its operating system. The company also acquired PowerPoint early on, turning the presentation software into another core part of its productivity suite.

According to Draper, this strategy allowed Microsoft to absorb successful ideas while the companies that initially popularized them gradually lost their competitive edge. He believes Bitcoin could follow the same playbook, with alternative cryptocurrencies serving as testing grounds for innovations that could eventually migrate to the Bitcoin network.

“Altcoins are the Lotus 1-2-3s and WordPerfects of this era,” Draper wrote, arguing that competing blockchain projects may demonstrate the value of new technologies before Bitcoin adopts them. In his view, Bitcoin’s powerful network effects and growing ecosystem could give it the gravitational pull needed to attract innovations from across the broader cryptocurrency industry.

Draper further supported his argument by highlighting Bitcoin’s expanding share of the overall cryptocurrency market. The billionaire recalled watching the flagship cryptocurrency’s market dominance climb from approximately 40% to 50% and eventually reach 61%. He views this steady increase as evidence of Bitcoin’s growing influence and its ability to strengthen its position despite the emergence of thousands of competing digital assets.

“Bitcoin is that platform,” Draper asserted.

If his prediction proves accurate, established altcoins such as Ripple-linked XRP, Dogecoin (DOGE), and Solana (SOL) could face an increasingly challenging competitive environment. Each has built its reputation around distinct use cases and communities, but Draper’s argument suggests that Bitcoin could eventually incorporate innovations that currently give these competing networks their appeal.

For instance, XRP is best known for its focus on cross-border payments and the expanding financial ecosystem built around the XRP Ledger. Dogecoin, meanwhile, has evolved from an internet meme into one of the cryptocurrency market’s most recognizable assets, backed by a dedicated community. Solana, on the other hand, has established itself as a major smart contract platform, attracting developers with its high transaction speeds and relatively low fees while supporting a diverse ecosystem of decentralized finance (DeFi), NFTs, meme coins, and tokenized real-world assets.

Ultimately, Draper’s thesis is that these innovations could be a boon for BTC rather than guarantee the long-term dominance of the altcoins that pioneered or popularized them.

#5202. Grvt wants to make RWA perpetual trading costs easier to plan for. Here’s how

Log in to access your notifications and stay updated. If you’re not a member yet, Sign Up to get started!

Sara is steadily working on cryptocurrency evaluations, news, and fluctuations in digital currency prices. She is guest author associated with many cryptocurrencies admin and contributes as an active guide to readers about recent updates on virtual currencies.

Sara is steadily working on cryptocurrency evaluations, news, and fluctuations in digital currency prices. She is guest author associated with many cryptocurrencies admin and contributes as an active guide to readers about recent updates on virtual currencies.

A trade can move in your favour and still leave you with a loss. The difference often comes to the spread between the buy and sell prices and unpredictable funding payments on perpetual contracts.

Grvt’s Stable Funding Perps (SFP) are designed to address both costs, starting with real-world commodities. Its gold contract XAU/USDC lets you take a long or short position on gold without an expiry date. Trades and funding settle in USDC on Grvt’s self-custodial platform.

Instead of relying on a crypto-native order book, SFP uses quotes from market makers who hedge their exposure in traditional markets. Grvt charges no trading fee or additional spread, although the market makers’ quotes still include a spread.

As for the funding, it can change during the day but it is applied only once at the weekday market close, based on the rate in effect at that time.

In this guide, we’ll walk through a gold trade to show how SFP works, from opening a position and understanding the spread to calculating funding and checking the payment in Fee History.

The first step is to enable Multi-asset margin on your Grvt account which allows you to use USDC and USDT as collateral, although SFP trades and funding settle in USDC.

On the Grvt trading page, open your trading account’s mode settings and select Multi-asset margin if it isn’t already enabled. You can then check your available collateral and make sure you have sufficient margin to open a position.

Open the instrument selector and choose Stable Funding Perps then XAU/USDC.

Unlike crypto perps, which generally trade around the clock, SFP follows the trading hours of the underlying traditional markets.

Most of the launch markets are structured to be trading for around 23 hours a day and five days a week, although there are exceptions such as Brent which has shorter hours.

The trade screen interface also features a countdown making it easy to track markets open and close. What’s worth keeping in mind though is that your position remains open and liquidation is still possible if your account falls below its maintenance margin requirement.

Grvt uses a request-for-quote (RFQ) model whereby market makers provide live Buy and Sell prices, with the difference being the spread.

To provide some more context, let’s say gold is quoted at 3,001 USDC to buy and 2,999 USDC to sell. Buying and immediately selling one unit at those prices would cost 2 USDC even if gold’s market price hadn’t moved.

Grvt charges a 0% trading fee and doesn’t add its own markup to the market maker’s spread. You still pay the spread built into the quotes, however, so check the prices for the size you want to trade. Larger orders may receive different quotes.

The spread tells you what entering and exiting costs. Funding determines what you pay or receive for holding the position through the market’s weekday close.

Unlike conventional crypto perps, where funding generally helps align contract and reference prices, SFP links funding to market makers’ financing costs in traditional markets, with an adjustment applied by Grvt.

Check the rate for your side in the funding bar:

The displayed rate can change throughout the day. If you’re still holding at the close, Grvt uses the rate then in effect and the full position value to calculate funding.

Metals have 3x funding on Wednesday, while oil and gas have 3x funding on Friday to account for the weekend. Funding also settles on weekday holidays.

Suppose your gold position is worth 3,000 USDC at Wednesday’s close.

At an annualised funding rate of –3.65%, your estimated payment is:

But if the rate changes to −7.30% by the close, you pay:

Your holding cost has doubled despite the position value remaining unchanged.

Always check whether Grvt displays a daily or annualised rate. The Funding tab can show a 24-hour rate, while annualised rates must be divided by 365 before applying the appropriate multiplier.

The final step is to enter a position, either go long (buy) or go short (sell). Key in the size you want and leverage; and make sure it is above the minimum order size. Once done, you can review the quote again before confirming.

Most launch markets allow up to 20x leverage, while silver is capped at 10x. Larger positions may have lower limits.

For market orders, set your slippage tolerance but also understand that an unfavourable price change can result in a partial fill or no fill and market makers can also reject an order at the final quote check.

Once filled, check your entry price under Positions. To exit, review the opposite-side quote and close the position while the market is open. You can then check Fee History for funding debits or credits.

Before you open an SFP position, estimate how far the price needs to move for you to break even. Use the spread for your order size and the funding you expect to pay or receive over your holding period. Revisit that estimate if the quotes change or you decide to hold through another close.

#5201. Bitcoin Demand Dries Up as Miners Prepare to Dump 2,077 BTC: Is More Selling Pressure Coming for BTC?

Bitcoin demand weakens as miners transfer 2,077 BTC to exchanges; Antpool accounting for 97% ahead of an estimated 8% mining difficulty cut.

Bitcoin (BTC) demand is showing signs of weakness as miners move more coins to cryptocurrency exchanges. CryptoQuant recorded 2,077 BTC in miner-to-exchange transfers on November 10, approximately 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. The move comes as Bitcoin struggles to regain momentum and the network approaches an estimated 8% reduction in mining difficulty.

The latest figures raise concerns about potential selling pressure, particularly as demand indicators weaken across spot and derivatives markets.

Meanwhile, miners could soon receive some relief from lower network difficulty.

Bitcoin's Rebound Fades as Spot Demand Weakens and Miner Flows Surge

“Leverage is being unwound, but spot demand has not recovered sustainably.” – By @xwinfinance pic.twitter.com/n03axjQKqt

— CryptoQuant.com (@cryptoquant_com) November 13, 2026

Explore: Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $69,000: Is the Worst Still to Come?

The 2,077 BTC transfer marked the largest daily miner-to-exchange movement since February 2026, according to CryptoQuant. Around 97% of the transferred Bitcoin came from Antpool, one of the network’s largest mining pools.

The movement represents a significant increase compared with the 30-day average of 127 BTC. Miners often transfer Bitcoin to exchanges when they need to liquidate holdings to cover electricity bills, equipment costs and other operating expenses.

However, CryptoQuant’s Miner to Exchange Flow indicator tracks transfers rather than completed sales. Miners can also move coins for treasury management or other operational reasons.

The latest activity therefore signals a potential increase in available selling supply, rather than confirmation that 2,077 BTC entered the market as sell orders.

Miner transfers are adding to concerns about an already fragile market. CryptoQuant’s 30-day demand-growth indicators showed negative readings across both spot and perpetual futures markets.

Spot demand stood at approximately -280,000 BTC, while perpetual futures demand reached around -82,000 BTC. Combined, the indicators produced a negative reading of approximately 362,000 BTC.

These figures point to deteriorating demand conditions. Spot demand is particularly important because it reflects activity in the underlying Bitcoin market, while perpetual futures activity provides insight into speculative positioning.

The negative readings suggest that buying activity has struggled to absorb available supply. If miners continue transferring Bitcoin to exchanges while spot demand remains weak, the market could face additional downward pressure.

However, these indicators measure changes in estimated demand, not a direct count of Bitcoin sold by investors.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Bitcoin’s next difficulty adjustment, expected around 14 November at block 975,744, may drop by roughly 8.4% after average block times rose to 655 seconds. The protocol reduces difficulty every 2,016 blocks (about two weeks) to maintain a 10-minute target; slower production eases mining and may boost BTC yield per unit of power.

This could aid miners amid weak prices and tight margins, but profitability still depends on electricity costs, hardware efficiency, fees and BTC value.

#5200. Binance Warns About AI Scams

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has warned of the rising risk of AI scams, including the use of deepfakes that impersonate Binance executives and staff.

The world's largest crypto exchange recently took to X to warn its users that improvements in artificial intelligence are making it harder to distinguish fake messages from real ones.

"AI deepfakes are making impersonation scams harder to spot," the crypto exchange said in a post.

The cryptocurrency exchange has assured its users that no one from Binance will ever reach out to them asking for money or offering unsolicited investment advice.

Binance says scammers are making realistic deepfake videos featuring executives and employees of the company.

Fraudsters are using these deepfakes, some of which are very realistic, to trick potential targets through fraudulent video calls.

That way, people who fall victim to the scam might think they are interacting with real Binance personnel.

Binance warned that scammers often try to reach potential targets through messaging apps such as WhatsApp or Telegram. They impersonate Binance employees by using their names, photos, and job titles to appear credible.

After making contact with a potential victim, the scammer may try to convince them to send crypto, take part in an exclusive investment opportunity, or take other financial actions.

Binance has called on crypto users to be cautious about any unexpected messages they receive, even if they seem to be from someone at the company they know.

A realistic appearance no longer guarantees a person's identity, given that AI can now easily mimic voices and facial expressions.

Users should double-check any suspicious messages through official Binance support channels before taking any action.

#5192. Brazil Takes Aim at Stablecoins With Shocking Money Laundering Claim

The head of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil has claimed that legitimately obtained money could be considered laundered if it’s used to purchase stablecoins.

The senior Brazilian official claimed that converting money into stablecoins could link it to money laundering, even when it was initially obtained legally.

According to a recent report, Gerson Romantini, who is the director of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil, allegedly made the controversial statements at a private event attended by representatives of financial companies.

Romantini claimed that funds acquired legally could be transformed once they enter the stablecoin ecosystem.

In his view, even legally obtained money could effectively be "dirtied" if used in certain stablecoin schemes, and thus be considered part of a money laundering operation.

It’s important to note that the comments attributed to Romantini do not represent an official statement that all conversions into stablecoins could be considered money laundering.

This statement comes as Brazil has already moved to tighten restrictions on how cryptocurrencies are used for international payments.

On April 30, the Central Bank of Brazil published Resolution No. 561, which took effect on Oct. 1.

The resolution limits the use of virtual assets for the settlement of international payment and transfer services, also known as eFX.

In practice, this means that payments between an eFX provider and its foreign partner must be settled through traditional foreign exchange operations or a Brazilian real account opened by nonresidents.

Crypto payments for these particular settlements are off-limits.

A practice called the "stablecoin sandwich" is particularly concerning.

The way it works is that a Brazilian fintech accepts a certain amount of reais from a customer, then uses this money to purchase stablecoins like USDT or USDC and sends the funds in crypto to an offshore company.

This company, in turn, can convert these stablecoins into fiat currency to make payments or send money to families.

This allows users to make international money transfers for a lower fee and circumvent some of the infrastructure banks use.

The controversial statements have already received a response from Brazil’s crypto industry.

In a statement on Nov. 14, the Brazilian Association of Tokenization and Digital Assets (ABToken) questioned the alleged classification of stablecoin transactions as money laundering.

ABToken maintains that the use of stablecoins is not necessarily illegal.

Furthermore, the association also cautioned that sweeping bans may create legal confusion and hinder legitimate business activities that use stablecoins for international payments.

Charles Hoskinson has credited the underlying architecture for keeping Cardano (ADA) and Midnight (NIGHT) unaffected by the recent Binance hack, arguing that years of deliberate design decisions are now paying off.

The Cardano founder acknowledged that the network’s early focus on emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, liquid non-custodial staking, and the need for Layer-2 (L2) solutions built around its Extended UTXO (EUTXO) model, came in handy during the hacking incident.

Cardano’s staking model continues to grow, with the Cardano Foundation reporting that 57.6% of ADA’s circulating supply is staked.

Notably, every delegated coin backs a stake pool that helps produce blocks and secure the network.

Unlike traditional staking models that lock up assets, Cardano’s liquid staking allows holders to delegate their ADA while retaining full control. As a result, they can spend, transfer, or move their funds without first having to unstake them.

Therefore, this approach is unique because it combines network participation with financial flexibility while supporting a decentralized pool ecosystem. Additionally, it reduces reliance on centralized custodians, boosting the network’s broader resilience.

Meanwhile, Cardano is expanding its real-world utility since police in Uttar Pradesh, India’s most populous state, recently began using its blockchain technology to track forensic evidence in active criminal investigations.

More importantly, the Cardano Foundation said evidence scans and laboratory results will be recorded on-chain, creating a tamper-resistant audit trail designed to strengthen the integrity of investigations.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has published a lengthy post on EIP-8037, a change planned for the Glamsterdam upgrade. In his latest post, Buterin wrote that something like EIP-8037 is, unfortunately, the only way for Ethereum to scale safely.

With the update, Ethereum will collect an additional gas fee for the creation of new accounts. Creating a new account would cost more than five times as much gas as it does now, with new storage slots and contracts getting more expensive too.

According to Buterin, execution is easy to scale, but Ethereum's state already grows by around 110 GiB per year, and every node has to keep it.

Unfortunately, it will bring more pressure on existing contracts, for example, the OP Stack bridge. The bridge has a hardcoded gas limit of 40,000, and even a small increase in state gas costs would push its operation above it. Mainnet has at least 13 contracts like that, according to the security firm ChainSecurity.

It's a double-edged sword: from one standpoint, it limits the ability of spammers and scammers to fill the network with junk accounts used by illicit actors; from the other, it creates additional financial pressure.

Glamsterdam being postponed is another pain factor here: considering the poor state of the market and Ethereum's struggle, it's clear that any delays in major updates negatively affect the network outlook. The new date is yet to be confirmed.

Vitalik Buterin has been hinting at the change in gas consumption for ages now. Back in 2024, he called multidimensional gas the hardest problem in his own post on the topic.

Setting strict limits was never a farsighted option, and developers have been told that for years. However, it's yet another question: who's actually to blame? Buterin himself admitted that this rule hasn't been written down or repeated since 2021, so newer developers simply didn't know about it.

He now suggests writing down a list of features that are likely to change, from gas mechanics to slot time.

#5186. How AI Assistants and PrimeXBT MCP Could Change Crypto Trading Workflows

A crypto trader checking in at any hour may want to know how close their account is to liquidation, what is moving right now, or what the next order will cost. Answering those questions often means jumping between tabs, charts and calculators, while an AI assistant can handle most of that legwork.

PrimeXBT, a global multi-asset broker and crypto asset service provider, is introducing a new way to simplify these routine tasks through Model Context Protocol (MCP), a technology that connects AI assistants with external platforms and live data. With PrimeXBT MCP, traders can connect AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Codex, Claude or Claude Code to their accounts on broker’s PXTrader 2.0 trading platform, allowing them to access account information, monitor markets and prepare orders using everyday language.

From monitoring positions and analysing market movements to preparing orders and understanding trading conditions, MCP supports a range of everyday trading activities. Here are some practical ways crypto traders can use it.

Traders can start with account monitoring. Instead of opening the positions tab, a trader can ask “How close is my account to liquidation?” and the assistant replies with the account’s margin figures and lists the open positions with their stop-loss, take-profit and estimated liquidation levels. How liquidation works depends on the margin mode. In cross margin, all open positions share one pool of margin and liquidation is judged on the whole account. In isolated margin, each position has its own margin and can be liquidated on its own.

For market information, a trader may ask “What are today’s top movers?” and the assistant returns the markets that moved most in the last 24 hours, with the price, the percentage change and the volume traded. Volume matters in crypto: a big jump on thin trading doesn’t always mean many traders are behind the move. The assistant can also give the live price the account actually trades at, with the sell and buy side, and charts from one minute to one month.

Placing an order starts the same way: describe it in a line and the assistant prepares it. PrimeXBT works out the price, order cost, margin, fee, leverage and liquidation price, the assistant shows them on an order card, and nothing is sent until the trader presses Confirm. Each confirmation works once and expires after about a minute. The assistant can also help change leverage, move a stop-loss or take-profit, cancel an order or close a position, with a preview first each time.

4. Understand Trading Conditions Through Plain-Language Explanations

Margin, leverage and liquidation can be confusing for newer traders, and a misunderstanding can be expensive. The assistant can explain each one in simple words, using the figures on the trader’s own order card, instead of a definition from a help page.

AI-assistant can also say why an order was rejected. If the reason is not enough free margin, for example, it says so and suggests reducing the quantity or adding funds. Without the assistant, the trader would be searching the help pages for the answer.

Together, these capabilities show how MCP can simplify everyday trading activities, from routine account checks to more informed trade preparation.

“AI is becoming a more practical part of how traders interact with financial markets. With technologies like MCP, we’re moving towards a future where traders can manage more of their daily activities through a simple conversation, from checking positions to preparing orders. What’s important is that the technology makes trading more accessible and efficient, while traders remain in control of every decision,” said Jonatan Randin, CMT – Senior Market Analyst at PrimeXBT.

The assistant doesn’t trade on its own and doesn’t make decisions. Traders connect their own AI assistant, rather than using one provided by PrimeXBT. When connecting, the trader picks Read only or Read and trade for one account and can switch access off whenever they like. The connection can’t be used to withdraw or transfer funds. AI assistants can also make mistakes or decline certain requests, but traders can always access their accounts and manage trades directly through the PXTrader 2.0 platform. Traders should also keep in mind that market prices can change between order preview and execution, so the final execution price may differ from the estimate shown.

MCP isn’t built for scalping, meaning very fast and frequent trading, or for bots that run around the clock. For traders who prefer automated strategies, PrimeXBT also offers a Trading API that supports algorithmic trading, with API keys, two-factor authentication and optional IP restrictions. MCP, on the other hand, is for traders who prefer to ask questions, review their positions and prepare orders through an AI assistant, with each trade requiring their confirmation.

Setup involves one link and a PrimeXBT login, with no API keys to create or copy. In the assistant, the trader adds PrimeXBT as a custom connector, signs in, chooses the account and access level, and clicks Allow access. Some assistants have their own requirements: ChatGPT, for example, needs Developer mode. MCP works with PXTrader 2.0 only, not MT5.

Adding PrimeXBT as a custom connector in Claude. Other assistants follow the instructions on screen.

For crypto traders interested in trying MCP, a PrimeXBT demo account is a practical place to start. They can connect an AI assistant, ask about their balance or open positions and see how it responds using their own account data before deciding whether to use it on a live account.

Looking ahead, integrations like MCP could change how crypto traders interact with their accounts, particularly in a market that operates 24 hours a day. As AI assistants gain access to more financial tools and live data, everyday tasks such as monitoring exposure, reviewing trading costs and preparing orders could become easier to manage through a single conversation. PrimeXBT’s integration of MCP marks another step towards a more accessible and intuitive trading experience, bringing AI-powered tools closer to the everyday needs of crypto traders.

PrimeXBT is a global multi-asset broker and crypto asset service provider trusted by traders in more than 150 countries. The platform bridges traditional and digital markets within one integrated environment, redefining versatility and innovation in online trading. Clients can access Forex, CFDs on indices, commodities, shares, crypto, and Crypto Futures, as well as buy, store and exchange cryptocurrencies. This unified experience extends across both the native PXTrader 2.0 platform and MetaTrader 5, supported by advanced risk-management tools and a wide range of funding options in crypto, fiat and local payment methods. Since 2018, PrimeXBT has focused on empowering traders through broad multi-asset access, fair and transparent conditions, professional-grade technology and dedicated human support. By combining expertise, trust and a client-first approach, PrimeXBT sets a benchmark of excellence in the financial industry and provides traders with the tools they need to trade, grow and succeed with confidence.

#5183. Bitcoin May Never See a New ATH Again, Peter Brandt Floats Grim Scenario as Bearish Pattern Emerges

Bitcoin investors may have witnessed the cryptocurrency’s final record-breaking rally, at least according to veteran trader Peter Brandt. The legendary chartist has sounded the alarm over a potentially massive bearish pattern emerging on Bitcoin’s weekly chart, warning that if the formation holds, the apex crypto’s October 2025 all-time high above $126,000 may never be surpassed in his lifetime. His alarming assessment comes as BTC reels from a brutal market downturn, adding fresh uncertainty to an already battered crypto market.

Peter Brandt has raised the possibility that Bitcoin may have already reached its ultimate price peak after spotting a potentially significant bearish formation on its weekly chart. In a November 15 post on X, the renowned chartist questioned whether BTC was developing a legitimate head-and-shoulders (H&S) top, a technical pattern often associated with a major trend reversal.

Brandt suggested that if the formation proves valid, he could construct a technical case that Bitcoin’s previous record high was its last, potentially remaining unbeaten for the rest of his lifetime. His warning is particularly striking given that Bitcoin reached a record of $126,080 in October 2025 before suffering a sharp correction.

The H&S formation typically features three peaks, with the middle one (the head) rising above the two surrounding peaks (the shoulders). The pattern is considered bearish when the price breaks below the neckline, which connects the two troughs separating these peaks. Such a breakdown could signal weakening buying pressure and open the door to further losses. In Bitcoin’s case, the asset is approaching a crucial support zone between $60,000 and $65,000, which could serve as the neckline of the potential bearish formation.

However, Brandt has not confirmed that Bitcoin has completed this formation. His assessment remains conditional on whether the chart structure represents a legitimate bearish reversal, meaning traders will likely watch the potential neckline for signs of confirmation.

Bitcoin has extended its recent decline, with selling pressure intensifying on Nov. 13 as the flagship cryptocurrency dropped below the psychologically significant $70,000 threshold for the first time since August. The latest downturn has deepened its weekly losses to approximately 14.8%, highlighting the growing bearish sentiment weighing on the broader crypto market.

Meanwhile, crypto analyst James Check has pointed to another worrying development, suggesting Bitcoin is experiencing its fourth capitulation event since reaching its all-time high. According to Check, daily realized losses have surged, doubling from about $420 million to more than $850 million in just 24 hours.

Check also offered a more optimistic perspective, arguing that Bitcoin has entered what he describes as a “deep value” zone. He noted that the cryptocurrency last traded in similar territory in February and late June this year, with the previous comparable occurrence dating back to the 2022 crypto bear market.

However, the pundit cautioned that entering this zone does not necessarily mean Bitcoin has reached its market bottom. Instead, he suggested that investors who begin gradually accumulating BTC at these levels could eventually benefit if historical patterns repeat, potentially turning the current market weakness into a long-term buying opportunity.

#5182. Major Wealth Advisor With $24 Billion in Assets Discloses XRP ETF Stake

Major U.S. wealth management company EP Wealth Advisors has revealed that it holds an investment in an XRP exchange-traded fund (ETF). This was disclosed in the company's latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

EP Wealth Advisors, a California-based investment advisory firm with about $24.4 billion in securities holdings, has revealed that it held 18,400 shares in the Volatility Shares XRP ETF (XRPI) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

This was disclosed in the official SEC filing that the company submitted to the commission on Nov. 13. The filing showed that the investment was valued at $147,936 at the end of the third quarter.

Furthermore, the filing showed that the total portfolio value reported by EP Wealth Advisors stood at $24,380,879,896. This value comprises 1,603 items in the company's 13F information table.

It's worth noting, however, that this isn't the company's total assets under management. It's the value of its reportable securities holdings. There are also assets that are not included in Form 13F.

Interestingly, this isn't the first time EP Wealth Advisors has held an investment in XRPI. Data from its historical 13F filings shows that in the second quarter of 2026, the wealth management company held 13,425 shares in XRPI.

The recent filing shows that the company has now increased the number of shares it holds in the XRP ETF by 4,975 shares. This represents about a 37% increase in the company's XRPI holdings during the third quarter.

Nevertheless, this amount is very small relative to the company's multibillion-dollar securities portfolio. It represents less than 0.01% of the total value of its reported securities holdings.

It's also worth reiterating that Form 13F is simply a filing that shows institutional holdings at the end of a quarter. It doesn't necessarily represent the investment manager's current holdings.

The Volatility Shares XRP ETF was launched in May 2025. Its ticker symbol is XRPI, and it is currently trading on Nasdaq.

XRPI isn't a spot XRP ETF. This means it doesn't directly hold the cryptocurrency XRP. Rather, it primarily derives its exposure to XRP's price movements through XRP futures contracts.

This ETF essentially provides investors with a way to invest in XRP without actually having to hold or custody the cryptocurrency. The ETF aims to deliver investment returns that correlate with the performance of XRP.

As of Nov. 13, the most recent available data from the fund issuer shows that XRPI's net assets stood at about $77.9 million.

Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has replied to XRP holders who criticized him for selling most of his XRP with a Saturday Night Live GIF of Natalie Portman saying, "I never said I was a role model."

According to Schwartz, his XRP holdings are down 88%, from a peak of roughly 26 million tokens to 3 million. His Bitcoin went from about 1,500 coins to one, and his Ether went from about 40,000 to six.

Schwartz wrote that he "really doesn't like risk." According to Schwartz, he and his wife agreed years ago to sell some of their coins every time crypto reached a new all-time high. In 2025, Schwartz sold around 2.5 million XRP and paid about $1.7 million in capital gains tax on the sale. He had received these tokens in 2020 and 2023.

@hllywd22 @tchdwntommyd @WHTBOYRICKY @CryptoTaxFixer When XRP hit 10 cents, that seemed ridiculous. When ETH hit $1, that seemed ridiculous. What BTC hit $200, that seemed ridiculous.

Schwartz said that all of his sales were made under written trading plans, and a lawyer approved each plan at least 30 days before each sale. According to Schwartz, his largest risk asset is still his stake in Ripple.

Schwartz also said that he was a skeptic from the start and did not believe in the early price records of crypto. "When XRP hit 10 cents, that seemed ridiculous. When ETH hit $1, that seemed ridiculous," he wrote.

In his view, the price of XRP today depends on overall sentiment in the crypto market, and fees on the network barely move it. Schwartz allows that the token could capture some of the value of a successful ecosystem in the future, but there are no guarantees. On Monday, the price of XRP stands at $0.956.

On Nov. 16, Schwartz also posted a review of the XRPL codebase by the Qwen AI model. "I asked Qwen to rate my work on the XRPL software. It was mostly good. But this was harsh and it's not wrong," he wrote.

According to the review, the overall architecture of XRPL is good. Still, Qwen said that some components of the code are too tightly coupled, and the migration to a new testing framework stopped halfway. The AI model also called the code generation in XRPL opaque.

Several XRPL developers replied to the post and said that they are already rewriting some of these parts of the code. Other users asked for formal verification of the XRPL core before the new features planned for 2027 go live.

#5177. XRP Scams Soar Across Social Media, Here’s What To Watch Out For

Scam attempts aimed at XRP holders have reached intense levels, according to recent alerts from a well-known figure in the XRP Ledger community. Vet, a pseudonymous X account who also works as a dUNL validator while contributing to the XRP Ledger

Foundation has used his platform several times to highlight the growing threat.

In a recent check using platform data tools, he found that around 11.5 million posts directed at the XRP community appeared within a single 30-day stretch.

The vast majority dangled fake airdrops or reward schemes designed to trick people into handing over funds or linking their wallets. He described the sheer number as eye-opening and pushed users to stay highly alert.

Vet has also pointed out how quickly fraudsters react to genuine positive news. When real companies announce partnerships or integrations involving the XRP Ledger, scammers often rush to set up lookalike addresses and launch tokens that borrow those brand names.

His advice is straightforward: treat every unexpected offer with suspicion, and trust only details that come directly from the company’s official channels. In many cases, the real institutions never publish public issuer addresses.

He has spoken about the constant stream of scam tags that can make notifications almost impossible to manage. Seeing community members engage with these posts frustrates him, and he keeps returning to the same clear message. No one is giving away free XRP. The safest move is usually to ignore the approach completely.

Even specific token launches have drawn his scrutiny. After a large Japanese firm introduced a yen-backed stablecoin, Vet warned that any version appearing on the XRP Ledger under a similar ticker was almost certainly fake without an official issuer confirmation.

His ongoing posts underline a simple reality. Rising interest in XRP attracts more bad actors who try to cash in on the attention. For everyday holders, staying skeptical and double-checking everything remains the best protection.

#5172. From $2 to $60,000: The Eternal “Bitcoin Is a Scam” Timeline

As Bitcoin hurtles toward the $60k support level, critics are having a field day once again, calling it a scam and a pyramid scheme, among other things. However, one analyst noted that the digital currency has fallen every 4 years or so over the last 3 cycles, and the digital asset is simply following established trends.

The post documents that every major price drop has been met with triumphant celebrations over the digital currency’s demise. BTC has already dropped 50% from its all-time high (ATH) of $126.5k set roughly a year ago. While naysayers are having a field day right now, seasoned investors understand that the premier digital currency has a history of recovering well in the years that follow.

Bitcoin first experienced a major crash in 2011 when it dropped to $2. It was the first time it happened on such a noticeable scale, and many legacy analysts quickly declared it “dead” or a scam. However, Bitcoin recovered well and experienced a major bull run two years later that propelled it above $1,000 for a short while. This represented a 500x price increase.

Afterward, Bitcoin started to cool off again, and in 2015, the premier digital asset crashed to $250, sparking another episode of critics calling it a scam. However, the digital asset once again started to rise strongly two years after this occurrence and reached as high as $19,500 in late 2017, representing a 78x increase.

However, 2018 proved brutal for the cryptocurrency, and it dropped to sub-$3,000 levels near the end of the calendar year. Once again, the naysayers, led by Peter Schiff, were quick to declare it dead. The cryptocurrency remained on the defensive for about a year before beginning a major price recovery. By the end of 2021, Bitcoin had risen to $69k, representing a 23x price increase.

The 2022 bear market, like clockwork, soon followed, and the digital asset dropped to $15k, once again triggering critics. However, the bearish scenario eventually ended, and Bitcoin started to recover strongly in early 2024, resulting in a major price boom that pushed the cryptocurrency to $126.5k by October 2025, representing an 8.4x gain. Now, the digital currency is struggling above $60k and may likely fall even further below the key support. Critics are active, and in all practical purposes, this is peak FUD season.

Bitcoin’s recent troubles align with previous cycles, and it is important for long-term investors to stay patient and avoid panic selling.

#5170. Satoshi’s Bitcoin DNA in XRP Ledger Uncovered in Two Cryptographic Mechanisms

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. XRP Ledger Foundation Director of Community Hussein Zangana (Vet) shared a tidbit of XRPL's early history in a recent X post.

Vet noted that the XRP Ledger (XRPL) still carries traces of Satoshi Nakamoto’s original Bitcoin design, highlighting two features.

In 2011, three engineers—David Schwartz, Jed McCaleb, and Arthur Britto—began developing the XRP Ledger (XRPL). Fascinated by Bitcoin, they set out to create a better version that improved upon its limitations—with the goal of creating a digital asset that was more sustainable and built specifically for payments.

As reported, the first line of code for the core of what would become the XRP Ledger (XRPL) was written by David Schwartz, who is Ripple CTO emeritus, about 15 years ago, on November 11, 2011.

Vet delves into the earliest part of XRP Ledger history, noting that 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, wrote. Vet added that Jed McCaleb also copied Satoshi’s timekeeping code into the XRPL, even including one of the Bitcoin creator’s comments shared as a screenshot.

Did you know all of us on the XRP Ledger use design choices by Satoshi daily? 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Satoshi wrote. Jed copied Satoshi's timekeeping code into the XRPL, including one of Satoshi's comments. By the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone. In December 2014, Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment. Two design choices of Satoshi still remain on the XRPL and all of us use at least one of it. Signature curve secp256k1 (we also support Ed25519 thus not everyone uses this) and how XRPL addresses are generated from the public key with SHA-256 followed by RIPEMD-160, that's what all of us use.

The quote "Never go to sea with two chronometers; take one or three" is a classic maritime adage famously included by Satoshi Nakamoto (the pseudonymous creator of Bitcoin) within the Bitcoin source code.

Vet explained that by the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone from the XRP Ledger. In December 2014, former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment.

However, two of Satoshi's design choices still remain on the XRP Ledger: the first is the secp256k1 signature curve, which Bitcoin uses and which the XRP Ledger continues to support. However, the ledger also supports Ed25519, meaning not every XRPL user relies on secp256k1.

"I remember David saying they used secp256k1 so no one would doubt the security because it's the same as Bitcoin's, etc.," Vet stated, citing the insight of the Ripple CTO emeritus on secp256k1, adding, "Lots of interesting things to dig into from the early days."

The second is the method used to generate XRP Ledger addresses from public keys. The process applies SHA-256 hashing followed by RIPEMD-160, a design inherited from Bitcoin that remains common to all XRPL addresses.

Asked why the timekeeping code and Satoshi's comment were removed, Vet explained that this became leftover code as new code was introduced, so it was cleaned up.

Cardano DReps have rejected a proposal by Toto Finance to spend 22 million ADA from the Cardano treasury on a "Strategic Copper Reserve."

The vote closed on Nov. 15, and DReps holding 2.86 billion ADA voted against the proposal, according to Cardano governance data. DReps with 20.02 million ADA voted in favor of it.

DRep John MacPherson was among those who voted "No," and he explained his decision in a post on X.

MacPherson wrote that he is not against real-world assets on Cardano. Still, he said the proposal asks the treasury "to take on both the copper price and the ada price," and Toto Finance would collect "up to about 3.4M ada in fees."

At the same time, MacPherson said that the proposal is “more honest about its risks than most.”

Toto Finance, a company led by Monty Metzger, submitted the proposal on Oct. 15. ADA is trading at $0.152 on Monday, and the requested 22 million ADA is now worth around $3.3 million.

The plan was to buy copper with 14.72 million ADA and store it in a warehouse near New Orleans. Toto Finance wanted to issue one CuTT token for each pound of copper. The metal would be sold in 18 to 24 months.

The Cardano Foundation, which votes as a DRep, announced its "No" vote in October.

"We recognize the opportunity in real-world asset tokenization; however, this proposal places 22,000,000 ada under the recipient's sole control to fund a fee-heavy concentrated commodity position whose safeguards are not yet in place," the foundation wrote.

Three members of the Constitutional Committee voted "No," and the other four members did not vote.

Crypto commentator Ingeniero Cripto agreed with MacPherson in the replies under his post. He called the "double exposure" to the prices of copper and ADA the key problem of the proposal, as the Cardano treasury already holds ADA.

According to him, RWAs on Cardano make sense, but “funding the asset itself is a different question than funding the rails.”
